user_story: As a user I copy a folder to a destination so that it appears there under its own name
expected_behavior: A folder source lands as destination\folderName, nested files and subfolders are copied, exit code 0
evidence: folder copy nests the folder

user_story: As a user I merge a folder's contents into an existing destination instead of nesting it
expected_behavior: With -ContentsOnly the files land directly in the destination, no extra folder level is created
evidence: contents-only merges into the destination

user_story: As a user I copy one file to a destination folder
expected_behavior: The file is copied as destination\filename, exit code 0
evidence: single file lands in the destination folder

user_story: As a user I queue several sources in one run
expected_behavior: Every source is processed in order, each folder nests under its own name, exit code 0
evidence: several sources in one run

user_story: As a user I mirror a source so the destination matches it exactly
expected_behavior: Extra files in the destination are deleted, source files remain, exit code 0
evidence: mirror deletes extra destination files

user_story: As a user I am protected from accidental deletion when mirroring
expected_behavior: Mirror asks y/N and exits 3 on refusal; with -Quiet it refuses unless -Force is supplied
evidence: unattended mirror without -Force is refused

user_story: As a user I move instead of copy so the source is removed
expected_behavior: Files appear at the destination and the source copy is deleted, exit code 0
evidence: move removes the source

user_story: As a user I get proof the copy is intact
expected_behavior: Every source file is re-read and compared by SHA-256 after robocopy exits, exit code 0 when all match
evidence: clean copy verifies by SHA-256

user_story: As a user I re-check an existing backup without copying
expected_behavior: -VerifyOnly skips robocopy and compares source against destination, exit code 0 when all match
evidence: verify-only passes a clean tree

user_story: As a user I am told when a destination file does not match its source
expected_behavior: A missing or mismatched file produces a red per-file line, exit code 2, and a verify failure in the summary
evidence: verify detects a same-size corrupt file

user_story: As a user I keep empty folders in the copy
expected_behavior: Empty source directories exist at the destination after the copy
evidence: empty directories are preserved

user_story: As a user I copy files with non-ASCII names
expected_behavior: Files such as тест-文件.txt copy and verify without mangling the name
evidence: unicode filenames survive the copy

user_story: As a user I copy paths longer than 260 characters
expected_behavior: Paths over MAX_PATH copy and verify, using \\?\ for .NET calls and robocopy natively
evidence: a path longer than 260 characters

user_story: As a user I do not get infinite recursion through junctions
expected_behavior: Source reparse entries are excluded; destination reparse traversal is refused
evidence: test.ps1 junction exclusion and destination-junction refusal on both PowerShell hosts

user_story: As a user a transient lock does not abort the whole copy
expected_behavior: robocopy runs with /R:2 /W:2
evidence: code path present; not exercised

user_story: As a user I can tune copy parallelism
expected_behavior: -Threads N is passed as /MT:N
evidence: code path present; not exercised

user_story: As a user I see how far the copy has got
expected_behavior: A Write-Progress bar counts robocopy file lines against a pre-count of the source
evidence: code path present; not exercised

user_story: As a user I can inspect what happened after the window closed
expected_behavior: Each run writes bunshin-<timestamp>-<pid>.log under %LOCALAPPDATA%\bunshin\logs
evidence: each run writes a log

user_story: As a user I keep a record of a re-check
expected_behavior: -VerifyOnly writes a log with the destination, file count, failure count and each failure
evidence: verify-only writes its own log

user_story: As a user I can run it from another script without console noise
expected_behavior: -Quiet suppresses all Write-Host output while keeping the exit code and log
evidence: quiet mode prints nothing

user_story: As a user I can branch on the result in a script
expected_behavior: 0 success, 1 robocopy failure, 2 verification failure, 3 mirror aborted
evidence: exit codes are 0, 2 and 3

user_story: As a user a typo in the source fails loudly
expected_behavior: A non-existent source throws 'Source not found: <path>' before anything is copied
evidence: a missing source fails loudly

user_story: As a user I do not have to create the target folder first
expected_behavior: A missing destination is created for a copy
evidence: the destination is created for a copy

user_story: As a user a mistyped destination in a re-check does not create junk
expected_behavior: -VerifyOnly never creates the destination; missing files are reported
evidence: verify-only does not create the destination

user_story: As a user I see robocopy's file and byte totals
expected_behavior: Files and Bytes lines are read from the log and shown in the summary
notes: Regexes assume English robocopy output; localised Windows shows no summary

user_story: As a user Ctrl+C stops the copy and says so
expected_behavior: The run reports interruption rather than a normal summary
notes: Killing robocopy leaves the script to print its own summary

user_story: As a user I cannot ask for a guarantee the tool cannot give
expected_behavior: Move with -Verify or -VerifyOnly is refused with an explanation instead of failing verification
evidence: move plus verify is refused

user_story: As a user I add Bunshin to Explorer's Send to menu
expected_behavior: Install-SendTo.ps1 creates shell:sendto\Bunshin.lnk pointing at the script
evidence: sandbox install: quoted bundle path and real shortcut command

user_story: As a user I can undo the Explorer integration
expected_behavior: -Uninstall removes the shortcut and reports what it did
evidence: sandbox uninstall is idempotent and preserves unrelated shortcuts

user_story: As a user I pick a destination and get a verified copy from Explorer
expected_behavior: A folder picker opens, bunshin.ps1 runs with -Verify, and the console pauses with a readable result
evidence: bundled core tested; interactive Explorer selection and destination picker not driven

user_story: As a user who launched it directly I am told how to use it
expected_behavior: A yellow message explains the Send to workflow and the script exits 1
evidence: S01 executes actual shortcut command with no selection on both PowerShell hosts

user_story: As a user I drop files or folders on the window to queue them
expected_behavior: Dropped paths are added once each, regardless of which control they land on
evidence: built and launch-checked; interaction not automated

user_story: As a user I can pick sources without dragging
expected_behavior: Add files and Add folder open native pickers and append to the queue
evidence: 63-check UIA suite drives both native source pickers against portable executable

user_story: As a user I choose a destination and it is created if missing
expected_behavior: Browse opens a folder picker; Copy creates the destination folder
evidence: built and launch-checked; interaction not automated

user_story: As a user jobs run one at a time so disks are not fighting
expected_behavior: Each pending job runs copy then verify before the next starts
evidence: built and launch-checked; interaction not automated

user_story: As a user I can stop a running job
expected_behavior: Cancellation marks the job Cancelled; incomplete staging is removed and an existing destination survives a cancelled overwrite
evidence: public engine cancellation regression preserves old bytes; UIA cancellation keeps completed copy and reports verification incomplete

user_story: As a user I can see exactly which files failed
expected_behavior: Expandable results show File, Verdict, Size and Destination; selected rows expose copyable source and destination paths
evidence: portable UIA clean and same-size mismatch scenarios; screenshots inspected

user_story: As a user I can re-check from the GUI
expected_behavior: Exclusive Verify only mode skips copying and compares the source with the existing destination
evidence: portable UIA detects same-size mismatch and refuses missing destination without creating it

user_story: As a user I can mirror from the GUI
expected_behavior: Exclusive folder-only mirror confirms resolved targets; colliding plans are refused and extras are pruned only after a successful complete copy
evidence: portable UIA covers confirm/decline and unsafe plans; engine suite covers failed-copy and incomplete-scan guards

user_story: As a user I can watch one job's log without the others mixed in
expected_behavior: Each job writes to its own lane; the pane shows the selected job's lane, or the merged all-jobs view, capped at 2000 lines
evidence: UIA drives selected-job and all-jobs views; multi-job isolation and line cap not asserted

user_story: As a user I can go back to the full log
expected_behavior: Every job writes a unique gui-<timestamp>-<pid>-<id>.log under %LOCALAPPDATA%\bunshin\logs with verification and final outcome
evidence: GUI interaction suite asserts copy plus verify share one log; verify-only mismatch and cancellation records persist

user_story: As a user I see each job's state and the overall count
expected_behavior: Jobs show Queued, Copying, Verifying, Verified, Failed or Cancelled; explicit phases and prominent outcomes distinguish completion from verified success
evidence: portable UIA asserts completion, failure and cancellation summaries; rendered states inspected

user_story: As a user I can tidy up without losing running jobs
expected_behavior: Clear finished removes terminal jobs and clears the results table
evidence: portable UIA clears finished jobs and confirms mutation controls are disabled while busy

user_story: As a user I do not accidentally queue the same path twice
expected_behavior: An identical source path is ignored on drop or add
evidence: portable UIA adds the same folder twice and asserts one queue item

user_story: As a user I see how many bytes are left
expected_behavior: A determinate bar driven by CopyFileEx byte callbacks, with bytes done / total and MB/s shown next to it
evidence: 600 MB run showed 295/600 MB mid-file; a cancelled run left the bar partial
